context.before: To this end, instead of performing a single attention pooling, queries, keys, and values can be transformed with \(h\) independently learned linear projections. Then these \(h\) projected queries, keys, and values are fed into attention pooling in parallel. In the end, \(h\) attention-pooling outputs are concatenated and transformed with another learned linear projection to produce the final output. This design is called multi-head attention, where each of the \(h\) attention pooling outputs is a head (Vaswani et al., 2017). Using fully connected layers to perform learnable linear transformations, Fig. 11.5.1 describes multi-head attention.
